chunks: "The height of the Ka'bah was nine cubits, and it had no roof. Then Quraysh roofed it, making it eighteen cubits. Then al-Hajjaj demolished it against Ibn al-Zubayr, rebuilt it, and made it twenty-seven cubits."

key_terms.ابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ: Ibn al-Zubayr, in relation to whom the rebuilding took place
key_terms.الْحَجَّاجُ: al-Hajjaj, the ruler who later demolished and rebuilt it
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Ka'bah, the sacred sanctuary in Makkah
key_terms.ذِرَاعًا: a cubit as a unit of measurement
key_terms.قُرَيْشٌ: Quraysh, the tribe that rebuilt and roofed the Ka'bah

ai.seo_question: How did the dimensions and structure of the Ka'bah change over time according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports historical changes in the structure of the Ka'bah, describing its earlier height, the addition of a roof by Quraysh, and its later reconstruction by al-Hajjaj. Its significance lies in preserving details about the physical history of the sacred sanctuary connected with hajj.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2319 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The height of the Kaaba was nine cubits, and it had no roof. The Quraysh then roofed it, raising its height to eighteen cubits. Later, Al-Hajjaj demolished it during his conflict with Ibn Al-Zubayr and rebuilt it, raising its height to twenty-seven cubits."
